note: Golden examples for the Style Guide (docs/STYLE.md, 'Golden examples'). The player and the stray are the living staffs the owner chose on 2026-10-28 (docs/milestones/M2-living-staffs.md), each a body with its face as the game layers them. The others are the best placeholder art so far and are redrawn in that spirit over later milestones. The starter kit zip includes these files next to the palette and templates.
intro: The look: every character is a living staff, a body with floating eyes and brows; the rest is redrawn to match over time. Copy their approach, not their pixels.

examples.shows: A player character: a floating staff (the curl, player 1) pointing up and to the right, a Wood shaft with a Spark grip wrap, the player colour on the head only, the Optimist's eyes and neutral brows 8 px above the grip, drawn over the staff. The game draws the head sheet and the two face layers as three pictures; this is the three together
rules: player colour only on the head

examples.shows: An enemy, a stray (the Cinder Rod): a charred rod with a burning crown, no player colour, eyes glowing in fire's light shade with slit pupils, angry brows; the body and the face as the game layers them
A raised tile: lit top and left edge, shaded bottom and right edge
A flat tile: Stone base, a few inner details, nothing on the outer edge so it repeats
A projectile: a streak in Bone materials with a Spark core, outlined in its own shadow shade
An impact: a flat burst in Spark materials, over in 0.2 s
